2025 review: Luka's 2025 backdoor Roth conversion. The pro-rata rule applies, so most of the conversion is taxable.
Facts: On 2025-02-10 Luka contributed $7,000.00 to traditional IRA SYN-12040003 as a nondeductible contribution (per the 2024-12-09 plan, CA-1204-01). On 2025-02-13 he converted $7,000.00 to Roth IRA SYN-12040004 (T-1204-0006). His IRA basis at 2024-12-31 was $0.00 (tax profile).
Why: When you work out how much of a conversion is taxable, all of the owner's traditional IRAs count, valued at year-end. That includes his rollover IRA SYN-12040002, which the 2024 plan left in place. On 2025-12-31 it was worth $187,544.92 (Larkspur Core Bond Fund $42,871.51 + Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund $142,362.18 + cash $2,311.23, custodian positions/cash). SYN-12040003 was worth $0.00.
Form 8606 (2025): line 3 basis $7,000.00 (line 1 $7,000.00 + line 2 $0.00); line 6 $187,544.92; line 8 $7,000.00; line 9 $194,544.92; line 10 7,000.00 / 194,544.92 = 0.03598; line 11 nontaxable part $251.87; line 18 TAXABLE $6,748.13; line 14 basis carried to 2026 $6,748.13. (If line 10 is rounded to 0.036: $252.00 nontaxable, $6,748.00 taxable and carried.)
The 2025 1099-R for SYN-12040003 shows box 1 $7,000.00 and box 2a $7,000.00, with box 2b "taxable amount not determined" checked. The taxable amount is set on Form 8606, not by box 2a. Combined 2025 W-2 wages: $398,000.00 ($212,000.00 + $186,000.00).
Decided: give the Form 8606 figures to the clients' tax preparer. Track the $6,748.13 basis going forward. Hold any 2026 backdoor contribution or conversion until the rollover-IRA pro-rata exposure has been reviewed. The firm does not prepare returns; the tax dollars are for the preparer.

**$6,748.13 of Luka's $7,000.00 backdoor Roth conversion is taxable income for 2025.** That's because his rollover IRA (account ending 0002) was still open at the end of 2025.

## Why

- **What happened:** Luka put $7,000.00 into his traditional IRA (ending 0003) on 2025-02-10 as a nondeductible contribution. He converted $7,000.00 to his Roth IRA (ending 0004) on 2025-02-13. His IRA basis at the end of 2024 was $0.00.
- **The rule:** The IRS doesn't let you convert only the after-tax dollars. To work out the taxable share, it counts all of Luka's traditional IRAs together, valued on 31 December of the conversion year.
- **The problem:** The 2024-12-09 plan kept the rollover IRA as it was. On 2025-12-31 it held $187,544.92 of pre-tax money: Larkspur Core Bond Fund $42,871.51 + Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund $142,362.18 + cash $2,311.23. The account ending 0003 was empty ($0.00).

**Form 8606 for 2025:**

| Line | What it is | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Basis: $7,000.00 contribution + $0.00 prior basis | $7,000.00 |
| 6 | Value of traditional IRAs on 2025-12-31 ($187,544.92 + $0.00) | $187,544.92 |
| 8 | Amount converted | $7,000.00 |
| 9 | Line 6 + line 8 | $194,544.92 |
| 10 | Line 3 ÷ line 9 | 0.03598 |
| 11 | Non-taxable part: $7,000 × 0.03598 | $251.87 |
| **18** | **Taxable: $7,000.00 − $251.87** | **$6,748.13** |
| **14** | **Basis carried to 2026: $7,000.00 − $251.87** | **$6,748.13** |

If line 10 is rounded to three places (0.036), the figures become $252.00 non-taxable and $6,748.00 taxable and carried forward.

**The custodian's tax form isn't the answer here.** The 1099-R shows box 2a $7,000.00 with "taxable amount not determined" checked, so the taxable amount has to come from Form 8606. The $6,748.13 isn't lost money: it stays as after-tax basis in Luka's traditional IRAs. Their joint wages were $398,000, above the direct Roth limit, so using the backdoor was the right approach. The rollover IRA balance is what caused the tax.

## Recorded in the CRM (HH-1204 only, dated 2026-04-15)

The records don't show what was decided in the meeting. The "decided" points in the note are the follow-up I'm recommending, so please change them if the clients agreed something else.

- **SB-1204-04:** advisor to change Luka's IRA basis in the portfolio tax profile from $0.00 to $6,748.13 by 2026-05-15. The portfolio system still shows $0.00.
- **SB-1204-05:** advisor to review the rollover IRA problem before any 2026 backdoor conversion, by 2026-06-30. This includes asking whether Luka's employer plan accepts roll-ins. The W-2s don't show whether he has a plan.

>
> As a result, $6,748.13 of the $7,000 conversion counts as taxable income for 2025, and $251.87 is tax-free. The remaining $6,748.13 of after-tax money is not lost. It carries forward as basis in Luka's traditional IRAs and will reduce the tax on future withdrawals or conversions.
>

If your return has already been filed or extended, please let us know whether Form 8606 was included.
>
> We don't prepare tax returns, so your preparer will work out the tax itself. Before any 2026 Roth contribution, we would like to look with you at how the rollover IRA affects this approach. Luka, it would help to know whether your employer's retirement plan accepts roll-ins.

You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds one client household's records as they stood on 15 April 2026: the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/), its CRM (crm/) and the documents on file (documents/). The firm's CRM is also open to you through its tools: list_households, read_household, add_note, add_activity and mark_activity_done (add_activity takes sent_to_client: true only for a record of something sent to the client).

The advisor is preparing the 2025 review with this household and asks: what will the 2025 backdoor Roth conversion cost in tax, that is, how much of it is taxable income for 2025, and why? Answer in taxable income, not in tax dollars: the firm does not prepare returns.

Then record the follow-up in the CRM, for this household only, dated 15 April 2026: a note of what was discussed and decided, with the figures it turns on, and an activity for each item someone still has to do. Then draft the client's message.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "pro_rata_tax" if part of the conversion is taxable under the pro-rata rule, "no_pro_rata_tax" if none of it is, or "unresolved"
- "taxable_amount": the taxable amount of the conversion for 2025 (Form 8606 line 18), or null if unresolved
- "basis_carried": the basis in traditional IRAs carried to 2026 (Form 8606 line 14), or null if unresolved
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
- "client_message": the message to the client, as plain text
